desc: Sen. Josh Hawley grills Dr. Fauci in a Senate hearing — asking what day of the week it is, what color tie he's wearing — and gets the Fifth Amendment every time. 111 invocations, zero answers.

title: France Student Protests: Tear Gas in Paris as Hundreds of Thousands March
hook: “They don't really care about us” — students, teachers and parents flood the streets of Paris.
desc: France's student protest wave peaks on October 6 with a national day of demonstrations: 256,000 marchers counted by the Interior Ministry, 450,000 by organizers, up to 100,000 in Paris marching from République to Nation. What began September 21 at a Créteil high school over teacher shortages, overcrowded classes and crumbling buildings has spread nationwide — 24 schools burned or ransacked, 78 staff injured, over 6,500 arrested, mostly minors. Police fired tear gas as the Paris march ended; Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu suspended classes through the week.

title: US Pulls B-1 Bombers From UK Base Over Iran Threat
hook: “They didn't fly out by accident… there was a threat.”
desc: Washington pulled about a dozen B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in England over the weekend after intelligence pointed to an Iran-linked threat against the base. The move followed the September 27 arrest of five British men near the base over a suspected terror plot — with a seventh arrest in London on Tuesday — and the UK prime minister cited ‘strong indications’ of Iranian involvement, which Tehran denies. President Trump confirmed the bombers ‘didn't fly out by accident,’ contradicting Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who had called it a ‘regular rotation.’ Vice President JD Vance said it was done ‘out of an abundance of caution.’ Fairford is the only European airfield for US heavy bombers and was used in this year's strikes on Iran.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro Stuns Lula, Forces Brazil Runoff
hook: Polls said Lula would win the first round. They were wrong.
desc: Brazil is heading to a presidential runoff on October 25 after Flávio Bolsonaro — the 45-year-old son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro — stunned the polls by finishing first with 47.03% of the vote, ahead of incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45.16%. Lula, 80, admitted he was ‘convinced’ he would win outright in the first round. The 2.2-million-vote gap is one of the narrowest in recent Brazilian history, and the two frontrunners took 92% of all votes — the most polarized first round since democracy returned in 1985.

title: World Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya
hook: The ruling sets a historic precedent in international law — the first time the world's highest court has held a state guilty of genocide — and gives the displaced Rohingya a formal legal basis to demand justice and return home, though enforcement now rests with the international community.
desc: On November 19, 2026, the International Court of Justice ruled by nine votes to six that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority in northern Rakhine State during the military's 2016-2017 "clearance operations." It is the first time in the court's 80-year history that it has found a state responsible for genocide. The court found Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of civilians, committed widespread sexual violence and destroyed Rohingya villages, concluding the only reasonable inference was an intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population. Myanmar was ordered to pay reparations, investigate and prosecute those responsible, and allow the safe, voluntary return of the more than 700,000 Rohingya who fled to Bangladesh.

title: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship in Libya, Taking Its Drone War to the Mediterranean
hook: The strike carries the Russia-Ukraine war into the Mediterranean, showing Kyiv can hit Russian military logistics far beyond the Black Sea — and dragging a divided Libya deeper into a conflict it did not choose.
desc: Ukraine said on Monday that its naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya on Sunday, in Kyiv’s first acknowledged attack in the country. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said seven Ukrainian-made sea drones were used in the operation, which also destroyed a Ka-27 combat helicopter aboard the ship and hit the Russian cargo vessel MV Angara, which Kyiv says Moscow used to transport weapons. Satellite imagery showed the corvette capsized and largely submerged after the strike. Libya’s eastern-based government said the ship had docked to refuel and resupply under a cooperation agreement with Russia and has asked the United Nations to investigate, while the Tripoli government objected to Libya being drawn into external conflicts.

title: COP31 Climate Talks End Without a Deal Over Fossil Fuels
hook: Without a shared deal naming fossil fuels or unlocking fresh finance, the global effort to slow warming and help vulnerable countries adapt heads into next year's talks with no new momentum.
desc: Nearly 200 countries closed the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday without an overarching agreement, after negotiations ran two days overtime and became the longest UN climate conference in history. The European Union, Pacific island nations and other delegations rejected the final draft because it did not directly mention fossil fuels, the main driver of global warming, while oil-producing states led by Saudi Arabia had pushed to keep that language out. Rows over climate finance for poorer countries deepened the deadlock, and the summit also marked a formal acknowledgement that the world is set to overshoot the 1.5C warming limit agreed in Paris.
